Clock alignment, recalibration, joint read, and monotonic time estimation functions.

# Purpose
This file implements the `fd_clock` time-alignment logic. It defines the shared-memory state, object life-cycle functions, and update routines used to map one clock domain to another while keeping the estimated `y` time monotonic. The code stores epoch data, tracks recalibration parameters, and uses a filtered estimate of the clock rate to update the conversion from `x` ticks to `y` ticks. It also handles error cases where clock samples move backward or change rate outside the expected range, and it records those cases so the clock can recover.

The file exposes the main public API for the clock object: [`fd_clock_new`](<#fd_clock_new>), [`fd_clock_join`](<#fd_clock_join>), [`fd_clock_leave`](<#fd_clock_leave>), [`fd_clock_delete`](<#fd_clock_delete>), [`fd_clock_now`](<#fd_clock_now>), [`fd_clock_joint_read`](<#fd_clock_joint_read>), [`fd_clock_recal`](<#fd_clock_recal>), [`fd_clock_step`](<#fd_clock_step>), and [`fd_clock_strerror`](<#fd_clock_strerror>). It also provides size and alignment helpers, [`fd_clock_footprint`](<#fd_clock_footprint>) and [`fd_clock_align`](<#fd_clock_align>), for shared-memory allocation. The implementation uses a ring of epoch records in shared memory, sequence counters for safe concurrent reads, and recalibration math that updates the rate estimate and the effective `y` offset at each epoch.
